claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 5 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see that you have a 5-year-old son named Alex who lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and accommodation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for all of Alex's day-to-day care - I provide his food, buy his clothes, and he lives here with me full-time. I take care of everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK? And if so, do you have the right to reside here (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, or another immigration status)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm a UK citizen, so there's no issue with my right to reside here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? For example, Alex's other parent or another family member?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually part of the issue. Alex's other parent and I are both responsible for him, but we can't agree on who should claim the Child Benefit. We're both involved in his care, but we haven't been able to sort out between ourselves who should be the one to actually claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that situation. That's an important detail.

Let me ask you this to better understand the arrangement:

**Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he split his time between you and his other parent? And are you and Alex's other parent living together, or do you live separately?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me full-time - he doesn't split his time between us. His other parent and I live separately, but they're still involved in his life and we share responsibility for him. We just haven't been able to agree on who should actually claim the Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 5 years old (under 16) ✓
- He lives with you full-time in the UK ✓
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care and provide for his needs ✓
- You are a UK citizen living in the UK ✓

According to the Child Benefit rules, you would normally qualify for Child Benefit since you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. Alex lives with you, which typically means you're the one who should claim.

However, the rules are clear that **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Since you and Alex's other parent cannot agree on who should claim, the guidance states that **HMRC will decide who will get it** if you cannot agree between yourselves.

Given that Alex lives with you full-time and you provide his day-to-day care, you appear to meet all the eligibility criteria. The disagreement with the other parent doesn't make you ineligible - it just means HMRC may need to make the decision if you both attempt to claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the necessary criteria since you're responsible for Alex, he lives with you, he's under 16, and you're a UK citizen living in the UK.

Regarding the disagreement with Alex's other parent: you should proceed with your claim. If the other parent also tries to claim, HMRC will make the decision about who should receive it. Given that Alex lives with you full-time and you're providing his day-to-day care, you have a strong case.

**One important note:** If either you or your partner has an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.

You can make your claim online or by contacting HMRC. Would you like any other information about Child Benefit?
